item.description: Trump initially announced a 10 percent global tariff after the ruling, but later said he would raise it to 15 percent. The first 10 percent tariff took effect at the end of February.

item.description: Venstre leader and prime minister candidate Troels Lund Poulsen said Wednesday that religion should not drive immigration policy in Denmark, responding for the first time to the Danish People’s Party’s call for net emigration of Muslim citizens. “It is not religion that will determine how Danish immigration policy should be,” he said at a press […]

item.title: New bridge named after Queen Margrethe
item.description: Queen Margrethe has agreed to have the new Storstrøm Bridge named after her, according to a press release from the Danish Road Directorate on Wednesday. The new bridge, which connects Zealand and Falster, will be called Queen Margrethe II’s Bridge. The Danish Road Directorate is the contracting authority for the project. The bridge is expected […]

item.title: “American in inspiration, Danish in execution”: How an international and a local started their pie company
item.description: In central Copenhagen, there is a pie shop founded by Erin Chapman, an American, and Dorte Prip, a Dane. “When I came here, there weren’t that many foreigners,” Erin said. “So I mostly had Danish friends.” One thing is for sure: “Danes take time,” Erin says. “ It’s an investment to make a Danish friend, but it’s worth it.”

item.title: We live longer, but more live with chronic illness
item.description: Life expectancy has risen in Denmark, but a larger proportion of the population is living with long-term illness or health problems, according to the National Health Profile 2025. item.title: Maersk pauses bookings amid Middle East conflict
item.description: Maersk is temporarily suspending cargo bookings for several Middle Eastern countries, including Qatar, the UAE, Oman, Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia, due to regional conflict.
